title: Mt. Gox
creator: Bitcoin
deck: An exchange balance could look like money until the door to it stopped opening.
story: Rain runs down the glass, but the message behind it does not change. A customer stands outside with a piece of paper in hand. The screen says the withdrawal is pending; the chains say something worse. This is LORE’s imagined doorway into the collapse of Mt. Gox, where an ordinary action, taking out your own money, had become a question nobody could answer.

On 28 February 2014, the Tokyo-based exchange applied to the Tokyo District Court for civil rehabilitation, a form of insolvency protection. Its website had closed three days earlier. In its announcement, the company said approximately 750,000 customer bitcoins and 100,000 of its own had disappeared. These were preliminary reported figures, issued while the causes and extent of the losses were still being investigated.

The number on the newspaper therefore belongs to that first account of the crisis. On 20 March, Mt. Gox announced that it had located approximately 200,000 BTC in an old-format wallet, revising its estimate of missing bitcoin to about 650,000. The discovery mattered, but it did not turn the locked door into an open one. Customers had entered a legal process whose questions would take far longer to resolve.

The scene holds on that gap between a number on a screen and the ability to use it. Bitcoin could keep moving across its network while an exchange failed to return the funds in its care. For the figure in the rain, the distinction offers little immediate comfort. LORE places the promise of easy transfer beside a padlock, making custody and trust part of the collection’s story.

details.title: The first reported total
details.text: The newspaper’s 850,000 BTC refers to the initial missing amount. About 200,000 BTC were later located. The paper is fictional; its headline preserves the first report’s uncertainty.

details.title: The locked door
details.text: Chains, a padlock and the withdrawal-pending display turn lost access into a visible barrier. This is an imagined exchange entrance, not a likeness of a documented Mt. Gox building.

details.title: A paper plane stopped short
details.text: The white plane beside the chains recalls 007, The First Transfer. Its placement sets the collection’s image of money moving freely against this scene of waiting and obstruction.

details.title: An envelope from the future
details.text: The envelope marked 2024 looks ahead to Bitcoin and Bitcoin Cash repayments that July. It is an intentional, anachronistic collection clue, not mail present at the 2014 filing.

source_art_note: Mt. Gox’s [28 February announcement](https://www.mtgox.com/img/pdf/20140228-announcement_eng.pdf) records the civil-rehabilitation application and initial missing amounts; its [20 March update](https://www.mtgox.com/img/pdf/20140320-btc-announce.pdf) reports the old-wallet discovery. A [5 July 2024 trustee notice](https://www.mtgox.com/img/pdf/20240705_01_announcement_en.pdf) confirms Bitcoin and Bitcoin Cash repayments to some creditors. The card’s date marks a filing, not a one-day theft. The customer, rainy entrance and newspaper are fictional. WITHDRAWALS SUSPENDED is editorial copy; the 2024 envelope deliberately looks forward.

factual_qualifications: 28February is the application for civil rehabilitation, not the later formal commencement of bankruptcy proceedings.
850,000BTC initial company report; about200,000later found. Do not treat850kas the final loss amount.
Filing date does not establish the date or mechanism of a single theft. Do not repeat the company’s initial transaction-malleability explanation as settled fact.
Pending screen/fictional Tokyo scene symbolise inaccessible exchange custody; Bitcoin network itself did not stop.
10BTC lettering on plane is not reliably legible at card scale; clue prose identifies the plane without claiming text readability.

final_clue_metadata.meaning: Initial 2014 report, not the final loss total; approximately 200,000 BTC were later located
final_clue_metadata.visibility: Raised and readable in full card
